problem: Gate unpinned (mutation pass, research-evidence/mutation-1.json): removing the guard `if (at < 0) return undefined;` from handOffTarget (MetaprojectTree.tsx) survives the tree, view and platform suites. With the guard gone, an anchor that is not shown (the root's status row, whose anchor d: is never rendered, or an anchor that left in the same commit) no longer falls back to the old index; it picks the first row of the parent from the top of the tree (rows.slice(0)).
impact: No user-visible defect today, but the documented fallback for an unshown anchor ('none: the caller falls back to the old index') has no test, so a refactor could drop it and move focus to the top of the parent's rows without any test failing.
suggested_fix: Add a MetaprojectTree DOM test where the focused row's anchor is not shown: for example a focused root Loading/status row replaced by the root's first page, or an anchor removed in the same commit, asserting focus lands at the old index position. Confirm it fails with M3 applied.
evidence: mutation-1.json: M1 killed, M2 killed, M3 survived, M4 killed; M3 anchor `  if (at < 0) return undefined;` with an empty replacement; command and baseline (exit 0) recorded there.

premise.reasoning: The guard at MetaprojectTree.tsx:88 carries a documented contract, stated in the handOffTarget doc (:82-84) and in the layout-effect comment (:184-186): with no anchor shown, return none so that the caller (:192) focuses the row at the old index. It is the fallback branch of the operator's decision that 'focus goes to the row now at the same place' (journal, fix round 1). Without the guard, at = -1, so `after` becomes every row. With no parent, the result is rows[0]; with a parent, it is that parent's first row from the top of the tree. In the commonest cases this matches the old-index result: the root status row, whose anchor d:<root> is never rendered, is replaced at index 0. When no row of that parent remains, the result is undefined anyway, because rows[-1] is undefined. That explains why M3 survives. The mutant is still not equivalent. Take an entry whose anchor (the row before it) left in the same commit, as a new snapshot can do, at index > 0: with the guard, focus goes to the old index; without it, focus goes to rows[0]. So this is a real, reachable branch with a documented rule and no test. I found no intent signal or practice source against pinning it. Under the Iron Laws, a surviving mutant stays as reported unless intent or practice shrinks it. The suggested fix is sound: one DOM test with an unshown anchor at an index > 0, confirmed to fail under M3. It changes no behaviour.
